title: Group Behavior and Survival
seo_title: Group Behavior Worksheets: Flocks, Herds, Packs and Survival (High School Biology)
standard_text: Evaluate evidence for the role of group behavior on individual and species' chances to survive and reproduce.
meta_desc: Free high school biology worksheets on group behavior (NGSS HS-LS2-8): flocking, schooling, pack hunting, alarm calls, costs of group living and predator data. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Flocks, herds and packs raise each animal's chance to survive and reproduce.
body_html:
How to think about it

Groups help individuals survive and reproduce.

  • Benefits: spotting predators, confusing them, hunting big prey, sharing warmth and information.
  • Costs: more competition for food and faster spread of disease.
  • Use data (for example, predator success vs group size) to judge a claim.
Example

Hawk success: 1 bird 70%, 40 birds 10%. Safer?

Lower success = safer

Answer: the flock of 40

Example

Why do geese fly in a V?

Air flow behind the leader

Answer: to save energy

Common mistakes

  • Thinking animals form groups just to be friendly.
  • Forgetting that group living has costs.
  • Thinking bigger groups always mean less competition.

faq.q: Why do animals live in groups?
faq.a: Groups help them spot and confuse predators, hunt larger prey, stay warm and share information about food.

faq.q: Are there costs to group living?
faq.a: Yes. Group members compete for food and mates, and diseases and parasites spread more easily.
Look at data such as predator success or time spent watching for danger at different group sizes.
